text:
maria: Heads-up — found a weird fail case when converting HF jinja chat_template -> Redwood prompt. system role gets preserved but also leaked into the first user turn in some templates.

alex: ugh. do you have a minimal repro?

maria: yup. minimal HF jinja: 
```jinja
{%- if system %}
- role: system
  content: |
    {{ system }}
{%- endif %}
- role: user
  content: |
    {{ prompt }}
```
Converted by our converter => Redwood prompt we send: 
```text
[system]
You are a helpful assistant.
[system]
User: Tell me a joke about llamas.
```
Notice the system block repeated as a sentinel line right before the user message. That extra sentinel token is being tokenized as literal text by some models and confuses the assistant.

jon: does this happen for all models or only certain tokenizers?

maria: only seen on a subset — mostly older GPT-style tokenizers and some HF Llama variants where the tokenizer wasn't aware of the sentinel pattern. Also reproduced when running 4-bit quantized model in Dedicated (weirdly higher hallucination rate).

alex: could be our converter inserting a custom sentinel like `[system]` instead of mapping to Redwood's internal role framing. If tokenizer splits that into multiple tokens it might shift positions for kv-cache.

eva-bot: deploy-bot posted: conversion-runner v2.9.1 executed on 2026-03-18 16:22 UTC (id: conv-7843).

sarah: quick hack: wrap system in an explicit delimiter token that we add to the model's tokenizer vocabulary (e.g., `<|system|>`). but that's heavy for hosted models.

maria: tried adding `<|system|>` to tokenizer special_tokens via config.json and reran quant tests. 1) non-quant models: fixes prompt parsing, 2) 4-bit quant: still worse quality — hypothesis: quant kernel + tokenizer boundary change altered logits distribution at early positions.

alex: can you paste the small conversion function? maybe the bug is double-escaping or jinja whitespace handling.

maria: snippet: 
```python
def convert_jinja(jinja_str, mapping):
    out = jinja_str.replace('{% if system %}', '')
    out = out.replace("{{ system }}", mapping.get('system',''))
    out = out.replace("- role: user
  content: |
    {{ prompt }}", 'User: ' + mapping.get('prompt',''))
    return out
```
This naive replace ends up leaving leftover role markers in some templates. Also we collapse newlines which merges sentinel lines.

jon: try using the Jinja renderer instead of string replace (i.e., jinja2.Environment(...).from_string(...).render(...)). that should preserve whitespace control and not leave role markers.

maria: did that — fixed the sentinel duplication, but discovered another corner: some chat_templates include explicit special tokens in the prompt (e.g., ``). When we render, the tokenizer treats that as one token only if it's in the vocab; otherwise split. That explains the model mismatch.

alex: for onboarding checklist, propose: 1) render with jinja engine, 2) normalize role markers to Redwood format (no inline sentinel lines), 3) ensure any special tokens in templates are added to tokenizer special_tokens in config.json before tokenization, 4) run a quick eval (50 QA pairs) to catch early regressions, 5) for quant variants run separate smoke tests because quant amplifies token-boundary issues.

maria: added to onboarding doc + created small eval: 50 prompt-answer pairs, metrics: exact-match and helpfulness score. observed drop from 87% to 73% EM on 4-bit when sentinel unresolved.

jon: for short-term patch, can we post-process rendered prompt to remove duplicate system lines: regex like `(?s)(\[?system\]?\n){2,}` -> single instance?

maria: yes done, pushed conv-fix branch. it'll be in next canary. still want longer-term fix to not rely on regex.

alex: thanks. can we also add a unit test that simulates a jinja template with both `system` and an explicit `` token to catch tokenization regressions?

maria: yup will add tests and the 50-pair eval to the CI job. adding a note: when onboarding HF chat templates, treat any inline special token as "must-register" for tokenizer or replace with safe text.

sarah: nice investigative work team :thumbsup:

maria: filing a short issue with repro + patches: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-2912 (contains jinja sample, converter diff, and eval results).

alex: great — let's monitor the canary metrics after deploy. if canary shows spike in hallucinations revert conv-fix and roll forward with tokenization-vocab update.

maria: will do, tagging @oncall if canary > 10% regression.

(ends)
